headline: Islamabad to go fully cashless by December 31
subheadline: State minister says all ICT and CDA departments to stop accepting cash payments after November 30
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The federal government has decided to make Islamabad the country’s first fully cashless city, with December 31 set as the deadline.

Chairing a meeting in the federal capital, Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry said consultation and suggestions from all stakeholders are important for the successful implementation of the cashless Islamabad initiative.

The minister said no cash payments will be accepted at any department of Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) or the Capital Development Authority (CDA) after November 30.

He said the government aims to bring all merchants in Islamabad into the cashless payment system by December 31. He said around 26,000 merchants in Islamabad have already been connected to the digital payment system.

Talal Chaudhry said digital payment facilities will be provided at every level, from street vendors to major business centres.

Internationally, the shift towards digital payments continues to reshape urban economies, although the pace of adoption varies across countries.

Nordic nations remain among the world's leading markets for digital payments, with Sweden reporting particularly low cash usage.

Mainland China, meanwhile, relies heavily on QR-based mobile payment platforms, particularly Alipay and WeChat Pay, which are widely used for everyday transactions.

headline: Usman Nurmagomedov sentenced to six months in prison after attacking Merab Dvalishvili
subheadline: Khabib Nurmagomedov's cousin also faces hefty fine and deportation following Abu Dhabi hotel brawl
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Russian mixed martial arts (MMA) fighter Usman Nurmagomedov attacked the former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili and now the 28-year-old has reportedly been sentenced to six months in prison.

The videos of the incident went viral on social media and the people involved in the fight were arrested, including those who filmed the incident.

The Abu Dhabi Criminal Court on Friday, convicted 10 individuals involved in the altercation at a hotel on Yas Island.

According to The National, six individuals were sentenced to six months in prison, fined 300,000 UAE dirhams (approximately $82,000) each and ordered to be deported after serving their sentences.

Interestingly, two individuals who filmed and circulated footage of the incident received identical punishments for violating privacy laws.

Meanwhile, Dvalishvili and his friend Saba Lazishvili were reportedly released from custody after being fined 50,000 dirhams each.

Why did Usman Nurmagomedov attack Merab Dvalishvili?

The Georgian fighter was giving an interview in the lobby of the Yas Hilton hotel on Wednesday when Nurmagomedov and his associates approached him from behind.

Footage shows Nurmagomedov striking Dvalishvili, triggering a brawl that left the Georgian with a bloodied face.

The two camps have a history of animosity, with Dvalishvili having handed Usman's elder brother Umar Nurmagomedov his first professional MMA defeat at UFC 311 in January 2025.

Tension flared up again in July 2026 at a prior RAF event in Georgia, where Merab Dvalishvili slapped Akhmed Gadzhimagomedov, an associate of the Nurmagomedov camp.

Usman was in Abu Dhabi to support Umar ahead of his wrestling match against former UFC fighter Urijah Faber.

The prison sentence could potentially derail the Russian fighter's much-anticipated move to the UFC.

Nurmagomedov, who completed his Professional Fighters League (PFL) contract earlier this year, boasts an undefeated professional MMA record of 22-0.

headline: Prince William shares royal Christmas treat following Kate's carol announcement
subheadline: Princess Kate confirms date for sixth Together at Christmas carol service
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Prince William has shared a much-loved chocolate cake recipe with a touching link to Queen.

Princess Kate recently announced that she will host her sixth Together at Christmas service at Westminster Abbey on December 11, and William has offered a festive treat of his own by revealing the childhood favourite that became part of his wedding celebrations.

The Prince of Wales opened up about his affection for the classic chocolate biscuit cake in a feature for Country Life magazine, recalling how it became a familiar highlight of his visits to his grandmother.

“I definitely have a sweet tooth and I love this recipe, which was dreamt up by my grandmother’s kitchen team,” William said.

The cake was served alongside the traditional fruit cake at his wedding reception to Catherine in 2011.

He remembered how afternoon tea with the late Queen often came with the hope that his favourite chocolate creation would be on the menu.

“My grandmother got me into teatime with this cake being the perfect invitation,” he recalled.

“Every time I’d go to have tea with her, I’d be hoping it would be served.”

Although it was not offered on every visit, William said he was always delighted when it appeared, remembering the wonderful teas his grandmother would arrange.

He also told those occasions helped him develop a lasting appreciation for the British tradition of afternoon tea.

The cake itself has an impressive royal history.

Created with layers of Rich Tea biscuits held together by chocolate, the recipe was prepared on a grand scale for William and Catherine’s wedding reception at Buckingham Palace.

The three-tier creation was made to serve around 600 guests, with reports at the time describing it as a 40lb chocolate cake containing approximately 1,700 biscuits.

It was made by the Royal Family’s long-standing chocolate supplier, Barry Colenso.
